policy: reference configuration 27; BF16 stored tensors and FP32 reductions; scheduling studies do not measure the existing Fast application
numerical_scope: all generated request histories identical across paired arms in these retained traces; this does not assert equivalence with existing Fast arithmetic
statistical_unit: four paired whole-trace blocks per study; table quantiles are the median of each block quantile, with linear within-block quantiles; requests/tokens are dependent and never pooled as independent repetitions

offline.claim_scope: bounded offline makespan comparison under existing paired rule

online.claim_scope: descriptive short-trace arrival/latency distributions; no steady-state capacity or SLO verdict

pressure.claim_scope: bounded offline makespan comparison under existing paired rule

adaptive.calibration_residual_scope: descriptive residuals of all 2,544 dependent executed-step observations used for NNLS fitting; no independent-sample uncertainty claim
adaptive.coefficient_scope: zero fitted partition/logit coefficients do not imply zero physical cost; the fitted features can overlap in this workload
adaptive.target_scope: predicted synchronous execute cost; mandatory decodes/progress may exceed
adaptive.claim_scope: held-out short-trace predicted-execution budgeting tradeoff; no hard 25 ms guarantee, client SLO, goodput or default-policy promotion

findings: With 128 blocks, static, continuous and fixed 256-token chunking are faster than serial on the frozen offline trace under the predeclared paired rule. Median delivered throughput is 158.90, 158.51 and 149.31 versus 65.03 tokens/s.

Latency quantiles cross: offline fixed chunking has median block gap p95/p99 of 151.80/192.42 ms versus continuous 14.25/983.01 ms. Online at nominal 4 requests/s, fixed chunking has 133.86/183.67 ms versus continuous 12.56/371.14 ms. Smaller prefill chunks replace rare large stalls with more frequent smaller stalls.

The 40-block pressure trace regresses versus serial: chunked duration ratio is 2.37818, continuous 2.80546 and static 2.85532. Chunking preempts 57 times/block and executes 16,432 rows instead of 2,424; full-prefill batching preempts 62 times and executes 18,488 rows. This is evidence of expensive repeated history replay under the current admission/preemption policy.

Adaptive execution on the held-out trace at nominal 16 requests/s raises median paired duration by 24.97% and lowers median delivered throughput from 68.35 to 59.10 tokens/s, while median block token-gap p95/p99 falls from 244.28/278.96 to 24.15/24.98 ms. Self-control variation reaches 13.10%; all blocks and their variability are retained.
Every adaptive prediction is at most 25 ms, but 116 of 648 measured executed steps exceed 25 ms, with block counts 3, 2, 2 and 109. Median quantiles cannot establish a 25 ms SLO or reliable tail cap.

These are eight-request synthetic traces on one Apple M4 Pro/Metal device. They do not establish production serving, steady-state capacity, general model quality, arbitrary arrival-rate capacity, Fast-route speedup or asynchronous execution.
